operating_notes.text: Balu Forge subsidiary Naya Energy Works proposed renaming to Quantum Energetics Private Limited and altering its object clause to enter explosives manufacturing.
Secured maiden order in the aerospace sector from US-based Alpha Aircraft Systems Inc with advance received on May 25, 2026.
Secured initial contract for 30,000 units of 152mm artillery shells with potential to scale over 100,000 shells.

Preferential issue of ₹496.80 Cr comprised 45,00,000 equity shares (₹162.00 Cr) and 93,00,000 warrants at ₹360 each (₹334.80 Cr); 1,90,60,000 warrants converted and 74,00,000 outstanding as of March 31, 2026.
₹471.12 Cr of the ₹496.80 Cr preferential proceeds was utilised by March 31, 2026, leaving ₹25.68 Cr unutilised, all against the plant and machinery object.
Foreign subsidiary Safa Otomotiz FZE-LLC contributed ₹126.80 Cr revenue and ₹28.90 Cr net profit in Q1FY27, reviewed by another auditor.
Export receivables of ₹5.24 Cr from the wholly owned subsidiary are outstanding beyond RBI's prescribed realisation timelines.
The company has a single reportable segment: crankshafts and other forged components.
Defence, aerospace and railways accounted for ~50% of the order book in Q1FY27, up from 13% of FY26 revenue.
The 360,000 shells per annum large-calibre ammunition line at Belgaum has been commissioned and serial production of 152mm and 155mm shells has begun.
Quantum Energetics Private Limited, a subsidiary, plans to manufacture TNT, RDX, HMX and allied products subject to requisite approvals.
Defence/Aerospace/Railway rose to 34% of Q1FY27 revenue from 16% in FY25 and 36% in FY26.
Balu Forge received its first aerospace order from a United States customer, with no value disclosed.
Incremental orders for large-calibre artillery shells were received in Q1FY27.
Balu Forge received a multi-month contract for 155mm ERFB BB/BT shells from an Indian ammunition player following successful execution of 10,000-unit pilot.
Acquired ring rolling line with max 6.7 m outer diameter and 18,000 kg ring weight, adding 18,000 tons of heavy ring rolling capacity; production trial before end-2026.
EOGM passed FCCB issuance, ₹1,000 Cr borrowing limit and charge creation; public institutions voted 57.9988% against.

timeline.summary: On 25 May 2026, CFO Amit Ashok Todkari resigned for personal reasons and Sandeep Singh Chadha was named interim CFO from 26 May 2026.
Balu Forge's subsidiary approved renaming to Quantum Energetics and expanding its object clause into explosives manufacturing on May 25, 2026.
On May 26, 2026, Balu Forge Industries announced its maiden entry into the aerospace sector with a purchase order from US-based Alpha Aircraft Systems Inc.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹263.55 Cr, net profit ₹65.74 Cr.
On 1 June 2026, Balu Forge Industries announced an initial contract to supply 30,000 units of 152mm artillery shells to a major Indian energetics player.

On 12 August 2026 Balu Forge's board approved up to USD 60 million of FCCBs, a ₹1,000 Cr borrowing ceiling and security creation, to be put to shareholders at an EGM on September 04, 2026, alongside Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹300.71 Cr and PAT of ₹66.09 Cr.

On 12 August 2026 Balu Forge reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹300.71 Cr (up 29.0% YoY), EBITDA of ₹84.77 Cr (margin 28.2%) and PAT of ₹66.09 Cr, with defence, aerospace and railways at ~50% of the order book and an ICRA upgrade to A- (Stable)/A2+.

On 12 August 2026 Balu Forge reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹300.71 Cr (up 29.0% YoY), EBITDA of ₹84.77 Cr at a 28.2% margin (down from 31.0%) and PAT of ₹66.09 Cr, citing a maiden US aerospace order and incremental artillery shell orders.
On 17 August 2026, Balu Forge received a multi-month contract for 155mm ERFB BB/BT shells from an Indian ammunition player following successful execution.

On 3 September 2026 Balu Forge announced the acquisition of a ring rolling production line capable of forged rings up to 6.7 m OD and 18,000 kg, adding 18,000 tons of capacity, with production trials to start before end-2026.
On 04 September 2026, Balu Forge held an EOGM to approve FCCB issuance up to USD 60 million and increase borrowing limits to ₹1,000 Cr
On 4 September 2026; Balu Forge's EOGM passed all three special resolutions — FCCB issuance; ₹1,000 Cr borrowing limit and charge creation — with 99.82% of votes polled in favour
Balu Forge Industries Ltd’s Board, led by Managing Director Jaspal Singh Chandock, recommended a final dividend of ₹0.15 per share for FY2025-26 on September 7, 2026.
Balu Forge Industries Ltd filed its Annual Report for FY26 on September 7, 2026, including audited financial statements and notice of 37th AGM on September 30, 2026.
On 26 September 2026, Ms. Tabassum Begum resigned as Company Secretary & Compliance Officer due to marriage and relocation.

Balu Forge Industries Ltd’s 37th AGM held on 2026-09-30 via VC, with **Jaikaran Chandock** (Whole-Time Director) presiding and approving financial statements, ₹0.15 dividend, **Trimaan Jaspalsingh Chandock**’s re-appointment, and cost auditor remuneration ratification.

Jaspal Singh Chandock (MD) announced 37th AGM resolutions passed unanimously on 30th September 2026, including financial statements approval, dividend declaration of ₹0.15 per share, and cost auditor remuneration ratification.
